question: The marked price of an electronic watch in a store is ₹ 45,880 and it is available at a discount of 25%. What is the price (in ₹) that a customer pays if he buys it from the store?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Discount = 25% = 1/4

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) × (1 − 1/4) = 3/4 × MP

⇒ SP = 3/4 × 45880

⇒ SP = 3 × 11470

⇒ SP = 34410

**∴ The correct answer is ₹34,410.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 
• 
 Marked Price (MP) = ₹45,880 (100%)
 Selling Price (75%)
 Discount (25%)
 SP = ?
 1/4 of MP

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹45,880

Discount = 25%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 45880 × (100 − 25) ÷ 100

⇒ SP = 45880 × (75 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP = 45880 × (3 ÷ 4)

⇒ SP = 11470 × 3

⇒ SP = 34410

**∴ The correct answer is ₹34,410.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Discount Amount

Discount is a reduction given on the Marked Price (MP) of an article. Discount = MP − SP.

Marked Price vs Cost Price

The relationship between Cost Price (CP), Marked Price (MP), Profit (P) and Discount (D) is given by: MP ÷ CP = (100 + P%) ÷ (100 − D%).

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount percentage is (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.
